title: Isomorphic Words

concept.title: A one-to-one mapping needs two maps
body: Two words are **isomorphic** if you can replace the letters of the first word, always the same letter by the same letter, and get the second word. Different letters must go to different letters. So the mapping must work both ways: each letter of `s` has exactly one partner in `t`, and each letter of `t` has exactly one partner in `s`.

`setdefault` stores the pair the first time and returns the stored partner later. If the stored partner differs from the current letter, the words are not isomorphic. One map alone is not enough: `ab` and `aa` would pass if you checked only the direction `a -> a`, `b -> a`.

statement: Two words `s` and `t` of the same length are given. Print `yes` if the letters of `s` can be replaced one-to-one to give `t` (every letter of `s` always becomes the same letter, and two different letters never become the same letter), otherwise print `no`.
constraints: 1 <= length of s = length of t <= 20000
The words contain lowercase letters and digits.

examples.note: The letter o would need to become both a and r.
b -> b and d -> b: two letters would become the same letter.

hints: Each letter of `s` must always go to the same letter of `t`.
Also each letter of `t` must come from only one letter of `s`.
Keep two maps, one for each direction, and compare as you scan.
